It doesn't have to be a bike, and a bike doesn't help with your diet, which is what causes the weight gain.

For the exercise, just do "something". Anything is better than nothing. The motivation to get going is found by just doing something, anything. It won't be perfect. It won't be ideal. But it will be better than pidgeonholing yourself into one ideal. Want to try some crossfit? Most of it is just advanced boot camp style calisthenics. Go for walks, jog, swim, hell prancercise if it will get you moving. Just do something. By the way, whatever you're doing it's going to be wrong with the incorrect form. You'll get better. Your form will get better. You'll start doing the right things. You will progress, as long as you do something and work towards a goal.

Now, the weight thing. Eating is what causes it. Sure, doing no exercise definitely doesn't help. But you can't exercise away a bad diet. Look at what you're eating and try eating less of it in smaller portions. Think about the short gratification carbs like twinkies and cinnabon and think about how much better and filling some nuts a protein bar would be. Maybe even start tracking on a site like My Fitness Pal or Spark People. Weight gain is always from absorbing more calories than you burn. You won't do this right at first either. You'll have too much to eat one day, or the wrong things, or short yourself throughout the day and be super hungry by the end. Just keep going and learn from your mistakes. Just keep going.

that's awesome! How difficult was it to get Gentoo set up and properly configured for your laptops? If you don't mind me asking, how long did it take?

Not too long actually. I thing I spent more time reading the documentation and the wiki than doing the installation itself. Gentoo is very well documented, the install guide is easy to follow.

I think the mistake is to try to install everything at once. I took about 2 hours at the basic install (the installation guide) in each laptop. Then I left recompiling everything over night.

Then I install X (in the acer aspire with i7, it takes some 10-20 minutes, in the dell latitude with a pentium M, about 40 minutes - 1 hour). HerbstluftWM and xterm takes less than 5 minutes, it is fast. With just that I have a usable laptop an install programs as needed. I have the same approach to the kernel: I make a minimum kernel, and then go adding support for things as I need.

To compile Plasma 2, even in a good machine, takes a LOOONG time (I leave it overnight). QtWebKit alone takes more than 1 hour. GCC updates also take a long time. However, I don't need to wait for it to finish, I run the compilation at the background and can work normally in the machines, even in the pre-historic dell.

One of the most useful tips I saw was a kernel option (that - I think - is not enabled by default) to make the kernel export it's own config file in gz format at /proc/config.gz. That way, when there is a new kernel, I just "zcat /proc/config.gz > /usr/src/linux/.config". That way I only need to worry about new configuration options. Since most of the time the new options is for stuff I don't care/I don't have, I have a new kernel compiling in less than 10 minutes.

The history of life:

  1. Amino Acids probably formed into RNA, which at some point probably became encased in phospholipids, which probably at some point became the first primitive DNA resembling a virus, which at some point developed the ability to self-replicate- This was the first single celled organism.
  2. After a while, the single cell organisms developed the ability to photosynthesize energy from sun light and CO2 gas- this was the rise of the Clones- also known as prokaryote Cyanobacteria. All these single cell critters ruled the Earth for a few hundred million years and converted our atmosphere from a toxic volcanic waste shit hole, into the beautiful azure skies we all know and love.
  3. Eventually, one of the cyanobacteria was pushed too far down below all her lazy sister cyanobacteria, who spent all day lounging in the sun. The little critter didn't like being pushed down and started eating her sisters until she could lounge in the sun too- this was the rise of the Eukaryotes predators.
  4. Tired of being eaten, one day a few sisters decided to join together to form the first multicellular colony. This was the rise of cell specialization.
  5. Finding they could not hunt cell colonies very well and not wanting to be out done, a few sisters decided to become neural networks that could cause the cell colonies to detect and react to the world around them- this was the rise of the jelly fish.
  6. Discovering the power of neural networks, cell colonies decided to try out as many different possible body forms as possible- this was the Cambrian Explosion.
  7. There were a few extinction events and a few more lifestyles and forms tried out, until eventually hominids emerged.
  8. Hominids were hunted and didn't like it, so they remembered back to the time their single celled ancestors formed into colonies to ward off predators- this was the rise of tribes.
  9. Not wanting to be outdone by their cousins, some hominids emerged and decided that instead of using tribes only for protection, they could use tribes for hunting and gathering.
  10. Tired of constantly moving around hunting and looking for food in random places, humans emerged and decided to start domesticating their prey animals, bees, and planting the seeds of their favorite plants to eat.
  11. Tired of working with ungrateful farm animals or hard labor in the fields, a few humans remembered the time that their ancestors developed cell specialization. These humans decided to have humans specialize their labor for the sake of the colony- this was the rise of civilization.
  12. Not wanting to be out done, a few humans decided that they could exchange IOUs for specialized labor. This was the rise of the banks.
  13. Seeing that the IOUs were sometimes made by banks with empty vaults, civilizations decided to run on the banks and kill all the bankers- this was the rise of organized labor.

  15. Not liking usury, the people remembered back to the time when some of their ancestors became neural networks and the people invented object oriented computing to better control the bankers.
  16. Seeing that computers could make their jobs easier, the bankers decided to incorporate them into their usury systems.
  17. Not wanting to be outdone, a few people invented cryptocurrency to destroy fractional reserve banking.
  18. Not liking the imminent destruction of their usury systems, banks began making world trade agreements to control the flow of information.
  19. Unwilling to break the laws of the universe, principally the law that says one cannot exclusively own electron patterns- even by fiat- the people rebelled, merged with their computer networks, and became cyborgs.
